analysis.title: Market Update: US Midterm Election Results
key_insights: Democrats won a majority in both the House and the Senate in the US midterm elections, with a narrow Senate majority. Vontobel calls the scale of the shift historic: the last time a sitting president lost both chambers was 20 years ago.
Texas, Republican for nearly forty years, and Kansas, Republican for nearly 100 years, switched sides.
Initial market reaction: equities, US Treasuries and gold are higher and the USD is lower. The White House acknowledged the result and said it is willing to work with Democrats.
Markets assume the new Congress could slow some market-friendly initiatives of the administration. Greater budget and debt discipline is expected, which could support bonds.

Congress can now block initiatives on the budget, taxes and regulation. The White House is expected to keep using executive orders, especially on trade policy, but these often end up in court and are overturned. The President has announced he will use vetoes.
Democrats are expected to open investigations into alleged personal enrichment, government contracting and conflicts of interest.
Some political analysts see a risk of renewed escalation in the Middle East in the window before the new Congress is constituted in January 2027.

US equities have often posted positive returns in the 12 months after midterm elections, in every midterm since World War II. Vontobel notes that history does not allow conclusions about future performance.

Markets expect a Democratic Congress to slow growth through more regulation, tighter spending control and fewer tax breaks. A slowdown would also dampen inflation, and cost of living stays central politically.
Even with bond prices higher, money markets still expect the Fed to raise rates before the end of the year.
A government shutdown risk returns with greater budget discipline. Markets have grown used to it, but it still brings uncertainty.

Sector regulation risk is expected in artificial intelligence, banking and healthcare, including an attempt to roll back the administration's healthcare measures (relevant to Swiss pharma). Environmental and energy policy may affect AI data centers.

Positioning: Vontobel keeps its preference for equities, implemented through emerging markets, which it sees as having growth potential at moderate valuations. It stays overweight gold and funds both positions with an underweight in corporate bonds, where credit spreads are relatively low. It recommends high diversification and stable income sources.

Diversifier. With inflation declining and rates expected to fall in the medium term, the price could recover.
Credit spreads remain at relatively low levels. The underweight funds the equity and gold overweights.

macro_indicators.reading: Described as declining, with rates expected to fall again in the medium term
macro_indicators.interpretation: Underpins Vontobel's gold overweight. The cost of living and the fight against inflation stay high on the political agenda.

macro_indicators.reading: Government bonds trading at higher prices, meaning lower yields, after the election
macro_indicators.interpretation: Treasuries gained on expectations of greater budget discipline.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight emerging market equities and overweight gold, funded by underweight corporate bonds
trade_ideas.rationale: Emerging markets offer compelling growth potential at moderate valuations. Gold can recover as inflation declines and rates are expected to fall medium term. Credit spreads are relatively low.
trade_ideas.risk: Political and geopolitical uncertainty, Middle East escalation, inflation and cost of living.

risk_factors: Slower growth from greater regulation, tighter government spending and fewer tax breaks.
Government shutdown risk from budget disputes.
Possible Middle East escalation before the new Congress is seated in January 2027.
Persistent inflation and cost of living, which tighten refinancing conditions.
Regulatory pressure on AI, banking, healthcare, and energy and environment policy affecting data centers.
Executive orders on trade policy may be overturned in court, which adds policy uncertainty.
charts_described: Figure 1 shows price returns following midterm elections. Vontobel says US equities have often generated positive returns in the 12 months afterward.
vol_and_positioning: Vontobel recommends a high level of diversification and a selective focus on stable sources of income to stabilize portfolios during political and geopolitical uncertainty.
Overweights in emerging market equities and gold are funded by an underweight in corporate bonds.
geopolitical: Democrats won both chambers of Congress in the US midterms, which puts the Republican administration in opposition to Congress.
Political analysts raise the risk of renewed Middle East escalation in the months before the new Congress is constituted in January 2027.
The White House is expected to rely on executive orders for trade policy, which are often challenged in court and overturned.
Middle East developments, oil prices, inflation and cost of living could dominate the agenda in the short term.

tension_points.bull_case: Vontobel points to US equities often posting positive returns in the 12 months after midterms, in every midterm since World War II. Less uncertainty, fewer political experiments and greater budget discipline are seen as supportive of stocks and bonds.
tension_points.bear_case: Greater regulation, tighter spending control and fewer tax breaks could slow growth. Vontobel adds that historical observations do not allow conclusions about future performance.

theme_stances.key_argument: Political deadlock is historically a positive sign for equities, and one source of uncertainty has been resolved.
Emerging markets offer compelling growth potential at moderate valuations.
